title: The Clickety-Clack Line’s Hidden Advantage

lines.text: He saw gaps in a railroad every 39 feet,
lines.label: 39 Feet

voice_script: [curious] He saw gaps in a railroad every 39 feet, and 2 companies are racing to build a railroad along a canyon. Whoever finishes first gets the whole country’s business. And when his boss sees gaps between every single rail, his face goes purple: [angry] You’re wrecking my railroad. But he won’t close a single one. So the other company lays their rails end to end, perfectly smooth, and finishes first. Their trains glide across the canyon without a sound, while his go clickety-clack over every gap, and the newspapers start calling it the clickety-clack line. [mysterious] Then summer comes, and something weird happens. His gaps start shrinking. In May, you can fit a coin in them. By July, barely a sheet of paper. Meanwhile, on the perfect railroad, the rails have started groaning in the afternoon sun, pushing against each other like they want to get out. [suspenseful] And on the hottest day anyone can remember, his gaps finally close, rail touching rail. And halfway across the canyon, the perfect railroad kicks sideways like a snake, right as a train rolls onto it. Follow the channel for more.
